newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR says Kuok alliance 'very important'.
newsitem.headline: CSR says Kuok alliance 'very important'.

text.p: Building materials, aluminium and sugar group CSR Ltd said its alliance with Singapore-based Kuok group was very important to the company's Asian expansion.
"The relationship with Kuok is very important to us because of their basic understanding of the highest levels of the market and industries in Asia," managing director Geoff Kells told reporters.

"... also their understanding of the practical issues that need to be solved to be successful in Asia, so we can continue to work very closely with them and we are about to get another wave of value adding from our relationship," Kells said.

Kuok group headed by Robert Kuok, which has interests in hotels, beverages, real estate and commodity trading, formed an alliance with CSR in September 1995, when it invested A$125 million for a 20 percent stake in CSR's Asian operations.

"The reason why we see specific value added opportunities in Asia is that we have worked hard to get an infrastructure in place and we can see that we can build off very easily from what we have got in a low cost way," Kells said.
CSR has spent about A$600 million on building its Asian operations over the past three years.
"Our strategy was to get ourselves a position to actually build volume. We have now done that and we now need to get some reasonable profits out of that," Kells said.
CSR earlier reported a 36 percent fall in net profit after abnormals to A$212.2 million for the year to March 31, 1997.
The group's Asian operations reported a loss of A$8.3 million for the 1996/97 year, compared with a profit of A$0.5 million in 1995/96.
